title: Sparse-slot KV allocator and fragmentation mitigation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Continuous batching and heterogeneous request lengths create high churn in the KV cache. Short-lived prefix entries combined with large,long-lived generations result in GPU memory fragmentation, increased OOM risk for peak bursts, and elevated tail latency when compaction or eviction happens synchronously.

Goal: Introduce an allocation strategy and operational playbook that reduces fragmentation by at least 30-40% for mixed workloads, preserves 99th percentile token latency targets, and keeps compaction CPU overhead within acceptable bounds. This change should be compatible with Dedicated and Private deployments and expose knobs via the runtime config and Console.

Proposal summary: Implement a hybrid sparse-slot allocator with micro-slab and reservation layers: 1) Segmented micro-slabs: allocate KV entries into size classes (micro-slab buckets) aligned to common KV object sizes observed in telemetry (small: <=256B, medium: 256-2048B, large: >2KB). 2) Transient reservation pools: for continuous batching, allocate a small transient pool per worker that services short-lived prefix entries; entries promoted to the global slab only if they persist beyond a time threshold or repeated hits. 3) Time-windowed aging and batch-aligned reclamation: schedule background compaction and reclamation synchronized to batch windows to avoid mid-batch pauses. 4) Indirection layer & soft handles: use an indirection table for KV lookups so compaction can move/merge entries without invalidating callers; this enables incremental copy-on-write compaction. 5) Probabilistic hole stitching: on eviction, probabilistically coalesce adjacent free micro-slots to create larger contiguous spaces for hot large entries. 6) Hot/cold segregation & per-model quotas: maintain hot pools for high-access keys and cold pools for long-tail items; expose quota hints per model to avoid one customer monopolizing KV slabs. 7) Telemetry & heuristics-driven thresholds: automatically tune promotion thresholds and reservation sizes using access-heat metrics and tail-latency feedback.

Why this is different: Rather than a single global compaction pass or simple slab allocator, this design combines (a) transient per-batch pools to absorb churn from continuous batching, (b) size-class micro-slabs to reduce internal fragmentation, and (c) an indirection/soft-handle layer to allow low-latency, incremental compaction without blocking inference.

Trade-offs and risks: Increased allocator complexity and CPU overhead for managing indirection and background compaction; potential metadata memory overhead for indirection tables; edge-case where promotion thresholds might under- or over-promote causing transient memory pressure. Mitigations include conservative defaults, gradual canary rollout, and runtime-configurable knobs.

Instrumentation and success metrics: fragmentation ratio (fragmented_free_bytes / total_free_bytes) target <= 0.25, 99th percentile token latency unchanged within 10% of baseline, background compaction CPU <= 4% of inference CPU budget on p3-sized instance at steady state, reduction in OOM incidents by 60% for mixed workloads.

Backward compatibility and rollout: feature-gate behind runtime flag kv_allocator_v2, default disabled for Private install until validated. Rollout plan: unit tests + microbench harness -> internal canary on non-production region -> customer beta with opt-in -> gradual ramp to default.

Outcomes: expected to lower memory amplification for multi-model pods, reduce forced evictions during bursts, and make Dedicated capacity more predictable per-GPU.
decisions: Adopt micro-slab size classes derived from telemetry percentiles (small/medium/large)
Use indirection table to support non-blocking compaction and pointer-safe moves
Implement transient per-worker reservation pools to absorb high-churn short-lived KV entries
Expose promotion threshold and reservation size as runtime-config knobs; enable heuristic autotuning later
next_steps: Prototype allocator data structures and indirection in a branch (branch: eng/kv/allocator-sparse-slot)
Add synthetic microbench harness that simulates continuous batching workloads (short prefixes + long responses)
Instrument fragmentation and per-size-class telemetry endpoints
Run perf comparison vs current allocator under mixed workload benchmark (latency, fragmentation, CPU)
Prepare canary rollout checklist and console UI flag to toggle kv_allocator_v2

updates: 2025-11-14: Initial analysis completed — identified that ~42% of free regions are <512B causing inability to place medium entries during bursts.

2025-11-20: Proof-of-concept allocator implemented; micro-slab bucketing and transient reservation logic working in local harness. Early results show fragmentation ratio improvement from 0.46 -> 0.28 on synthetic mixed workload.
2025-11-27: Added indirection table prototype to branch; verified move-on-compact without invalidating active lookups in unit tests. Not yet optimized for metadata memory footprint.

2025-12-01: Running end-to-end perf runs against real request traces from 3 customers (sanitized). Observed 6% CPU overhead for background compaction at current defaults; 99p latency within 6% of baseline for most workloads. Need to tune promotion thresholds for chat-heavy traces.

2025-12-03: Opened internal RFC for allocator persistence semantics and Private deployment compatibility. Planning canary in non-prod region next week. Assigned Marco Li to lead implementation and Aisha to own telemetry and release coordination.
